title: askmycrawl — scraper
description: scraper service — metrics, traces, and logs in one place. Kafka-only microservice (no HTTP surface, see backend/apps/scraper/src/main.ts) with no Postgres table of its own, so this drops both the HTTP row and the DB row service-auth.json/service-job-manager.json have. Modeled on service-job-manager.json's Overview/Kafka/Node-runtime/Traces/Logs rows (same instrumentation, same query shapes, just job="scraper"). All panels verified against the live stack with a real crawl (info.cern.ch, 24 pages) before being added, per .claude/agents/devops.md's Grafana dashboard discipline — including confirming @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node's kafkajs AND aws-sdk instrumentation both produce real spans here ('process crawl-frontier', 'send crawl-frontier'/'send page-scraped', 'S3.PutObject', 'tcp.connect' all seen live in Tempo). A Redis/BullMQ-specific panel (queue depth, job counts) is still NOT included — bullmq doesn't appear to have matching OTel auto-instrumentation the way kafkajs/aws-sdk/ioredis do; nothing to query yet, not confirmed either way, flag before assuming.

panels.title: Messages consumed rate
panels.description: crawl-frontier — the only topic the Scraper's Frontier Consumer consumes. @opentelemetry/instrumentation-kafkajs's messaging.process metric.

panels.title: Messages produced rate
panels.description: crawl-frontier (re-published child URLs) + page-scraped combined, plus crawl-complete on whichever crawl this Scraper instance happens to finish last (docs/planning/03-crawler-scraper-indexing-plan.md §6) — messaging.send metric.

panels.title: Produce rate by topic
panels.description: crawl-frontier (children), page-scraped, and crawl-complete when this instance wins the completion race.

panels.title: Message processing time p95 by topic
panels.description: No error/status label exists on this instrumentation's metrics (unlike HTTP's status_code) — a fetch failure, a permanent 4xx, or a BullMQ retry all show up in the logs panel below, not as a labeled series here.

panels.title: Recent traces
panels.description: Click a Trace ID to open the full trace. Confirmed live: kafkajs instrumentation produces 'process crawl-frontier' root spans with 'send crawl-frontier'/'send page-scraped' child spans; aws-sdk instrumentation produces 'S3.PutObject' spans for the SeaweedFS blob writes; 'tcp.connect' spans show the outbound page fetches. Deliberately a table, not the native 'traces' panel type — that panel doesn't auto-run its query on dashboard load/refresh in this Grafana version (see service-job-manager.json's identical note); a table with the same TraceQL query behaves like every other panel type and refreshes normally.
